text:
maya: quick question — trying to template envs for the billing service. Values let callers pass service.secretName and service.secretNamespace. We're rendering envFrom with a secretRef, but envFrom/secretRef can't reference other namespaces AFAIK. Is there a recommended pattern so chart remains flexible? :thinking:

sam: correct, envFrom secretRef is namespaced to the pod's ns. You can't reference a secret in a different namespace from a pod. Two main options: sync the secret into the release namespace (ExternalSecret / secret-syncer) or change the chart to accept raw keys and allow callers to inject them another way.

olivia: another common approach is to use Helm's lookup to detect the secret and conditionally render. Example:

```yaml
{{- $s := lookup "v1" "Secret" .Values.service.secretNamespace .Values.service.secretName }}
{{- if $s }}
envFrom:
- secretRef:
    name: {{ .Values.service.secretName }}
{{- else }}
# fallback (optional)
env:
- name: BILLING_TOKEN
  valueFrom:
    secretKeyRef:
      name: fallback-token
      key: token
{{- end }}
```

olivia: but note lookup only helps you decide what to render at template time — it doesn't solve runtime race where ExternalSecrets writes the secret after Helm installs.

maya: ah ok. So what's the best way to avoid pods starting with missing envs because ExternalSecret hadn't synced yet?

andrew: a couple options:
- make the ExternalSecret operator create the secret in the same namespace as the release (preferred for simplicity).
- add an initContainer that waits for the secret to exist before starting main container. super simple and robust.
- use a Helm pre-install job hook that blocks until the secret shows up (but hooks can be fiddly).

sam: +1 for initContainer. Something like: 

```yaml
initContainers:
- name: wait-for-secret
  image: bitnami/kubectl:1.26
  command: ["/bin/sh","-c"]
  args: ["until kubectl get secret {{ .Values.service.secretName }} -n $POD_NAMESPACE; do sleep 1; done"]
  env:
  - name: POD_NAMESPACE
    valueFrom:
      fieldRef:
        fieldPath: metadata.namespace
```

sam: downside is it ties chart to having kubectl image or custom wait logic, but it's explicit and avoids flakiness.

olivia: minor templating note: avoid letting callers set `service.secretNamespace` and then silently ignore it. If you accept cross-namespace intent, document that you will attempt lookup to detect presence but the actual envFrom will use the release namespace. Or fail fast with `required` so deployers know to sync the secret.

maya: thanks. One more — we currently render `envFrom: - secretRef: ...` and also `env: - name: FOO valueFrom: secretKeyRef` in different conditional paths. Any preference?

andrew: envFrom is concise when you want all keys, but explicit env entries are better for clarity and for avoiding accidental key leaks. If you only need a couple keys, prefer explicit `env`.

olivia: also consider `optional: true` on secretKeyRef if you want pods to start even when secret absent. But that changes semantics so use with caution.

maya: PTAL @andrew @sam — I pushed a quick draft to the PR that: uses lookup to detect secret, falls back to explicit env keys if not found, and adds an initContainer guarded by values.service.waitForSecret. Can you eyeball? link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/charts/pull/412

andrew: LGTM, left tiny nits in PR. :thumbsup:

sam: tested the initContainer approach in staging; it solved the race for us. one note: the bitnami image pulls might be slow, consider using a tiny busybox with `kubectl` copied in, or `curl` against the k8s API with service account token.

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: helm template exit code: 0, values schema: OK, lint: 1 warning (use of lookup), security-scan: no issues found.

maya: awesome, thanks everyone!
